issues: The narration excerpt “The burden of Babylon” omits the verse’s comma; quotations must preserve punctuation exactly.
The narration excerpt “Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain” omits the comma after “mountain”; quotations must preserve punctuation exactly.
“I have commanded my sanctified ones” and “I have also called my mighty ones” omit commas present in the source; quotations must preserve punctuation exactly.

The narration excerpt “a tumultuous noise of the kingdoms of nations gathered together” changes the source wording, which reads “a tumultuous noise of the kingdoms of nations gathered together” only with a preceding clause and comma; as a standalone excerpt it is otherwise exact.
The narration excerpt “the day of the Lord is at hand” omits the source’s “for” immediately before it; as a shorter exact excerpt it is otherwise exact.
The narration excerpts are exact contiguous phrases, but the scene summarizes future prophetic effects rather than depicting them as events; visual staging should preserve that distinction.
The narration excerpt “to lay the land desolate” omits preceding source wording but is an exact contiguous phrase; the second excerpt is exact.
The narration excerpt “the sun shall be darkened in his going forth” is exact; the second excerpt changes the source’s “cause her light to shine” to “cause her light to shine.”
“I will punish the world for evil” omits the source’s following comma; quotations must preserve punctuation exactly.
The narration excerpt “the earth shall remove out of her place” is exact; prophetic language should not be treated as a specified physical mechanism.
The similes are handled conservatively as figurative and the quoted excerpts are exact.

Lettering must be an exact source quotation: 'Their houses shall be spoiled' is not verbatim in 2 Nephi 23:16, which reads 'Their children, also shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes; their houses shall be spoiled and their wives ravished.'
The scene omits verse 16, but it does not claim to cover the full passage; no alteration to the preceding scene’s chronology is apparent.
The excerpt “Babylon, the glory of kingdoms” omits the source’s comma after “Babylon”; quotations must preserve punctuation exactly.

The scene assigns the voice in “For I will destroy her speedily” an unidentified identity but presents it as a literal first-person voice; the source does not establish a speaker, and the narration must not invent one.

The narration quotation “For I will destroy her speedily; yea, for I will be merciful unto my people, but the wicked shall perish.” includes punctuation and wording exactly, but presenting it as narration makes an unstated speaker attribution ambiguous.
The scene combines prophetic imagery and later outcomes in one entry; it must not portray the forecast beasts, satyrs, dragons, destruction, mercy, or perishing as present-tense events.
